Its scary that our government is fighting encryption when at the same time they are trying to pass CISA in the senate. If there are cyber attackers everywhere trying to obtain data, why can't I encrypt what is important to me? Why is it the government's business? I used encryption the other day for medical record correspondence. It could be useful for businesses to protect intellectual property and information about meetings. I use it for email and you can bet my phone is encrypted in case it ever ends up in the hands of a crooked cop...not that I have any wrongdoing to hide. Interestingly, the biggest CISA backers are financial companies. And with the way the CISA bill is written, anything you say or do online, that can be interpreted as felony behavior (not just terrorist statements), can be reported by corporations to law enforcement. How the hell does that protect anyone's information, besides the protecting government's ability to gobble up more information? How does it protect against foreign cyber attackers let alone domestic cyber attackers? You know, we could be progressing toward a better, hyperconnected world with an internet of things, but no one wants that right now because corporations, government and law enforcement are too powerful and unethical in this information age. Unfortunately, with all the backdoors already known to be in everyone's devices, from smart phones to harddrives, they can get what they want anyway. Not to mention that after the Patriot Act expired, congress enacted the Freedom Act, which says any information given to a third party is not protected by the 4th amendment and is fair game for NSA spying. Despite this, it is still important to say no to CISA and yes to encryption. Spying is necessary for the US and other countries, but domestic spying was never intended to be a feature of our ever day lives. There needs to be dialogue about what is ethical and what is not.
